r.정치 구도: Oman has been ruled by the Al Said family since the mid-18th century, and the sultan is both head of state and head of government. The previous sultan, who took the throne in 1970, ruled for nearly 50 years and built the roads, schools and hospitals of modern Oman. He had no children and left the name of his successor in an envelope, and in January 2020 a cousin succeeded him as written. In 2021 the new sultan amended the Basic Law to create the post of crown prince for the first time, with succession passing to the eldest son. The Council of Oman consists of an elected Shura Council and a State Council appointed by the sultan. It can review bills and question ministers, but the government can reject its proposals, so its power is limited. There are no political parties. Protests over jobs and corruption broke out in 2011, and work for young people is still the biggest challenge. Most citizens are Ibadi, neither Sunni nor Shia, which fits a foreign policy that stays out of sectarian quarrels.

t.why: The southern shore of the Strait of Hormuz is Musandam, an Omani exclave, so the tanker lanes run through Omani waters. Unlike its Gulf neighbors it has long kept good relations with Iran, and it joined neither the 2017 boycott of Qatar nor the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen. That made it the place where the United States and Iran meet quietly. The secret contacts that led to the 2015 nuclear deal began in Muscat, and when nuclear talks resumed in April 2025 the first round was held there too. The 2026 war tested that neutrality. Iranian drones and missiles hit the ports of Duqm and Salalah, which US and British forces use, and people were killed. Oman summoned Iran's ambassador but did not break off dialogue. After the strait was closed it discussed passage with Iran and opened temporary shipping routes on its own side, charging no tolls.
t.rel: It sits on the southern side of the Strait of Hormuz and is known as a quiet mediator that talks to both Iran and the United States.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1974. Liquefied natural gas is South Korea's biggest import from Oman. Daewoo Engineering & Construction and Samsung Engineering carried out major parts of the 230,000-barrel-a-day refinery at Duqm on the Arabian Sea, which opened in February 2024. In 2023 a consortium led by POSCO Holdings won the right to produce green hydrogen at Duqm, with a plan to turn hydrogen made from sun and wind into ammonia and ship it to South Korea. The Cheonghae Unit, the Korean naval force protecting ships off Somalia, has called at Omani ports for supplies.
t.know: It was the center of an ancient trade route that exported frankincense.
etext: Oman is not a member of OPEC but takes part in the wider group's output cuts. Its reserves are smaller than its neighbors' and its geology is harder, so it was early to use techniques that inject steam or gas to push oil out. Most of its crude goes to China, and its gas is liquefied and sold to South Korea, Japan and others.

Duqm, Salalah and Sohar all sit outside the Strait of Hormuz, on the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman. Oman built a special economic zone, a refinery and a ship repair yard at Duqm on the argument that ships can still call if the strait is closed. Those ports were attacked in the 2026 war, yet they served as a substitute route for ports inside the Gulf.

Oman is handing out desert land with strong sun and wind to foreign consortia to build green hydrogen projects. To wean the budget off oil it introduced value-added tax in 2021 and will levy a 5% income tax on high earners from 2028, the first personal income tax in the Gulf.

A large share of the budget still comes from oil and gas, so public finances swing with the oil price. The young population is growing fast and jobs are short. The public sector cannot absorb everyone, so the government is pushing to fill private-sector jobs with citizens.
